hypotheses.justification: `hab` is used only in the proof. The conclusion is an a.e. statement for `volume.restrict (Ioc a b)`, so the case `b ≤ a` holds trivially. New proof: do `by_cases hab : a < b`. If `a < b`, run the existing proof. Otherwise `Ioc a b = ∅` by `Set.Ioc_eq_empty hab` (its argument is `¬a < b`, as the uses in Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/Basic.lean show). Then `Measure.restrict_empty` turns the measure into `0`, and `ae_zero : ae 0 = ⊥` makes any `EventuallyEq` hold, e.g. by `simp [Set.Ioc_eq_empty hab]`. The other hypotheses are genuinely needed. Without `hg`, take `g x = 1/(x-c)^2` with `(c-a)/(b-a)` irrational. Then every `g * sin(kπ(x-a)/(b-a))` is non-integrable near `c`, so every interval integral is 0 by the junk-value convention, yet `g` is not a.e. zero.
